key_insight: Machine-learned dynamics reveal that surface polarons on oxygen-deficient rutile TiO2(110) move far less readily than in bulk because surface pathways are constrained and vacancies trap excess electrons.
engineering_relevance: The work helps explain low electron mobility in porous rutile TiO2 and provides a scalable route to study charge transport and reactivity at reducible oxide surfaces for energy and catalytic devices.
method: Extended machine-learning-assisted polaron dynamics to a reduced oxide surface.
Ran nanosecond-scale finite-temperature simulations on oxygen-deficient rutile TiO2(110).
Compared surface vs bulk hopping pathways and mobility trends.
evidence_signal: The study uses several nanoseconds of dynamics across multiple temperatures to quantify polaron hopping and finds surface mobility suppressed by several orders of magnitude relative to bulk.
watch_item: The conclusions are specific to the modeled reduced TiO2(110) surface, so transferability to other oxide surfaces and vacancy configurations should be validated.
paper_title: Machine-learned dynamics of surface polarons at reduced oxide surfaces
